items.summary: OCBC announced on Nov 26 that it has added a new 100-tonne dedicated gold vault in Singapore to expand its physical gold business and meet growing demand for trading and custody services. The facility can hold some 8,000 large gold bars weighing 12.4kg each and serves OCBC's institutional clients as well as those of its private banking subsidiary, Bank of Singapore. Kenneth Lai, head of global markets at OCBC, said interest in physical gold has been strong since the bank launched its physical gold business in June, reflecting growing demand from clients seeking secure, Singapore-based solutions for their physical gold needs. OCBC declined to disclose how much physical gold it currently holds in custody or the number of clients it stores gold for but noted increasing interest among institutional clients and Bank of Singapore clients looking for long-term custody arrangements. The new vault complements Singapore's broader efforts to strengthen its position as a leading gold trading and distribution hub in the Asia-Pacific region, including OCBC being a founding clearing member of an over-the-counter gold clearing system that the Singapore Exchange is set to launch in 2027, and MAS launching a gold vaulting service for foreign central banks on Nov 10. The new facility comes as part of a range of physical gold offerings available in Singapore, including Lion Global Investors' LionGlobal Singapore Physical Gold Fund launched in 2025, the first home-grown physical gold ETF listed on SGX in March 2026, fractional gold and silver investments through the OCBC app, and exposure to physical gold through Great Eastern investment-linked policies.
items.title: OCBC Opens New 100-Tonne Gold Vault in Singapore

items.summary: Trade records from risk intelligence platform Sayari show that Alice Huang, former head of the Singapore-registered cloud computing firm Megaspeed International (formerly 7Road Holdings), held overlapping roles across two related entities involved in equipment transactions. Of the 105 trade entries associated with VFO — a Hong Kong company incorporated as VFO Health and Beauty in 2018 that later became VFO Consulting, then VFO International Group by 2024 — 90 named PT Megaspeed International Indonesia as buyer (equipment movements recorded between May 2024 and February 2026), while another 10 named Speedmatrix, Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary. A separate set of records tied to Megaspeed shows 13 entries naming VFO as the buyer from PT Megaspeed International Indonesia; these figures may not represent distinct shipments since a single consignment can contain multiple product entries. Many transactions occurred in 2024 and early 2025, when Huang was still a director of VFO but had stepped down from Megaspeed's board in November 2023 — raising questions about her role on both sides. Accounting scholar Themin Suwardy noted that related-party deals within corporate groups are routine
items.title: Alice Huang's Overlapping Business Roles in VFO and Megaspeed Raise Conflict-of-Interest Questions

items.summary: The University of Sydney has become the first major Australian university to require honours students to defend their work in oral assessments, extending a policy it introduced across bachelor's degrees since 2024 as universities respond to growing concerns that generative-AI tools undermine written research. The change follows no public reports of AI cheating among honours students; geosciences coordinator Kurt Iveson said the move was driven by management wanting to demonstrate secure assessment for external accreditation and social licence rather than any observed misconduct. Under the new rules, formats differ across faculties: history student Aidan Elwig Pollock faced a pass-or-fail 15-minute conversation worth nothing toward his grade while most marks came from his thesis, whereas engineering student Isabelle* (name changed) had an hour-long interview with five professors that accounted for 50% of her grade against a 20,000-word thesis worth just 20%. The shift has stressed students who are not used to speaking publicly, non-native English speakers, and those pursuing professional qualifications such as engineering, prompting Isabelle to call it
items.title: University of Sydney Mandates Oral Defenses for Honours Students Amid AI Concerns

items.summary: Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier argue that the recent elections revealed an urgent public demand for change driven by AI-related economic disruption, while Democratic leaders have failed to present a compelling plan on artificial intelligence. An October survey they cite shows 84% of voters say AI threatens American workers, 57% believe the Trump administration has not taken AI risks seriously enough or at all, and that 61% of Republicans also want stricter AI regulation alongside Democrats—framing it as one of few issues crossing party lines. Sanders and Schneier contend that to win the 2028 presidential campaign, Democrats must align around an AI policy agenda and enter Congress in January ready for immediate legislative action, including rejecting tech billionaires' campaign funds and barring members from stock trading. They propose a three-plank platform: curbing big tech's power by taxing large datacenter energy use (drawing on Massachusetts' pollution-prevention model and the UK example of over £200m in public guarantees), building AI as a publicly regulated utility with federally developed models, and giving workers control through codetermination—preferring Warren's Accountable Capitalism Act, which would give workers at least 40% of board seats, over El-Sayed's narrower proposal. They contrast this with the Trump administration's stated
items.title: Sanders and Schneier Propose a Three-Point AI Regulation Plan for Democrats

items.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has announced a phased archiving process for inactive applications under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, effective from November 30, 2026. The move aims to streamline the application pipeline as it works toward its target of installing rooftop solar systems in one crore households by March 31, 2027. The process applies only to applications under the non-ULA and non-bank loan categories; ULA-model applications are excluded from archiving. It follows a strong response to the scheme: more than 91 lakh applications have been received through the National Portal (covering both regular and ULA models), while around 68 lakh consumers have already benefited, yet many registered applications remain inactive at various stages.
items.title: MNRE to Archive Inactive PM Surya Ghar Applications Starting November 30

items.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), through the National Institute of Solar Energy acting as its scheme implementation agency, has invited proposals from power distribution companies to implement a National Distributed Energy Resource Management System across India. Launched on November 20, 2026, this closed competitive challenge is part of the Innovative Projects Component of the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana and targets utilities managing rooftop solar, battery storage, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and other distributed energy resources amid rapid adoption—reflected in daily installations exceeding 13,000 nationwide. The scheme was approved in February 2024 with a total financial outlay of ₹75,021 crore through FY 2026-27. Eligible applicants include state-owned, private and joint venture DISCOMs along with power departments operating distribution networks; each may submit one proposal covering at least one distribution division or larger area with significant distributed energy resource penetration. Selected proposals must demonstrate real-time asset visibility, improved generation forecasting, grid balancing, voltage management, congestion control, dynamic hosting-capacity assessment, and consumer participation through baseline assessments, measurable key performance indicators, and acceptance criteria across technical, commercial, consumer, and environmental benefits.
items.title: MNRE Invites DISCOM Proposals for INR 2 Crore National DERMS Projects Under PM Surya Ghar Scheme

items.summary: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced Tuesday that she is pausing both pending and issued state permits for Enbridge's plan to replace a segment of the controversial Line 5 oil pipeline beneath the Straits of Mackinac. The pause requires regulators at EGLE to answer questions about the full scope of the project's environmental threats, following this summer's Michigan Supreme Court ruling that tossed out a related tunnel permit on grounds that its review of environmental harms was too narrow. Whitmer stated her ultimate goal is
items.title: Michigan Pauses Line 5 Tunnel Permits After Supreme Court Ruling

items.summary: A new modeling study published in Environmental Research Letters estimates that the added power demand from U.S. data centers drove an estimated 650 early deaths across the country in 2023, with authors noting the impact would likely be greater today given rapid buildout. The researchers found that pollution often intensifies far from where data centers are located: Virginia-based facilities connected to a large regional grid could spur Midwest power plants to ramp up output, increasing particulate pollution linked to heart attacks, strokes, and lung disease. Coauthor Noelle Selin of MIT's Center for Sustainability Science and Strategy said people without nearby data centers may still be affected by the resulting emissions.
items.title: U.S. Data Center Power Demand Linked to Hundreds of Early Deaths

items.summary: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States held steady at 607 this week, according to new data published by Baker Hughes on Wednesday ahead of Thanksgiving; that figure is up 63 from the same time last year. The count includes 470 active oil rigs (up 1 during the period) and 25 gas rigs (down 1), with miscellaneous rigs unchanged at 10. Separately, EIA data showed weekly U.S. crude oil production reached a record for the fifth consecutive week, rising to 14.065 million barrels per day during the week ending November 20 from 14.032 million bpd the prior week and up 251,000 bpd year over year. Primary Vision's Frac Spread Count rose to 194 as it regained 3 of the 4 crews it had lost the previous week, placing it 15 above a year earlier. Regionally, active drilling rigs in the Permian Basin were unchanged at 277 (up 26 from a year ago), while Eagle Ford rig activity held at 50, up 11 from this time last year.
items.title: U.S. Rig Count Holds Steady as Oil Production Hits Fifth Straight Record

items.summary: The Department of War is in talks with General Motors, Ford Motor Company, Canadian parts supplier Magna International, and other auto supply chain manufacturers to convert civilian manufacturing capacity for military drone production. According to The Wall Street Journal, these discussions reflect a broader push to expand stockpiles of unmanned systems across all categories, emphasizing lower-cost, attritable drones that can be fielded at scale to replace expensive legacy platforms. GM is weighing production of drone motors and has shown the greatest interest in supporting military production; DoW officials have also met with Ford Motor Company and other manufacturers that could produce engines, actuators, sensors, and lidar for drone makers. According to The Wall Street Journal, there is a strong sense of urgency at the Department of War to expand domestic drone supply chains, reduce dependence on Chinese components, and build stockpiles, with plans to buy millions of drones in coming years. The WSJ reports that DoW officials see the annual US military drone market reaching $20 billion (q1) to $30 billion (q2), but note that many existing American drone companies lack the manufacturing capacity to meet this incoming wave of demand.
items.title: Pentagon Seeking to Convert Automakers for Drone Production

items.summary: During Amazon's Black Friday Sale, several products reached new all-time lows. Worx's 40V 20-inch Cordless PowerShare snow blower with two 20V 6.0Ah batteries dropped to $349.99 shipped — a $70 markdown off its $420 full price and below the $357 low seen at October's Prime Day event, marking an all-time low. Anker's SOLIX E10 Whole-Home Backup System started from an exclusive new $3,609 low on the standard 6kWh setup (module plus battery), using code 9TO5DEALS5 to beat Amazon by $190 and deliver a total of $690 in savings off its $4,299 regular price; other configurations ranged from $5,799 for the 12kWh two-battery system up to $9,798 with a Smart Generator. Velotric's Breeze 1 Cruiser e-bike came bundled with an extra battery and roughly $640 of free gear (rear cargo rack, fender set, rear pannier bag) for $1,699 shipped — its biggest bundle deal to date and tied to the model's prior low. Eve's Aqua HomeKit Smart Water Controller fell to $99.95 shipped, a $50 markdown that placed it just above its all-time low of $110. The EGO Power+ Nexus Escape 400W Portable Inverter reached $129 shipped — a $40 discount and the second-lowest price of the year after an October Prime Day dip to $123.
items.title: Amazon Black Friday Deals Hit New Lows on Snow Blower, Backup System, E-Bike and More

items.summary: A Denny's restaurant in San Jose, where Jensen Huang held conversations with his co-founders that helped establish what became one of the world's most valuable technology companies, sent a message to Nvidia's chief executive. The chain framed its communication as an invitation for Huang to return—described as 'your booth is waiting'—following a plaque controversy. According to the item, Denny's positioned itself as reminding Huang that he still has a place at the table.
items.title: Denny's Sends Heartfelt Message to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang After Plaque Controversy

items.summary: Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp has announced a new feature that allows users to schedule messages so they are sent at a chosen time rather than immediately. The update lets recipients prepare birthday wishes or exam good-luck messages in advance, and it addresses the inconvenience of needing a phone switched on for a message to be delivered.
items.title: WhatsApp Adds Scheduled Messaging Feature

items.summary: On Thursday (Nov 26), Asian trading partners pushed back against the US Trade Representative's latest proposal of headline tariffs between 20 per cent and 40 per cent on 14 major trading partners. Singapore said it was 'very disappointed' with proposed duties of up to 20 per cent, arguing its outward- and market-oriented economy does not protect a domestic market or subsidize manufacturing for export (METI). Japan called the move 'regrettable,' rejecting claims that it has structural excess production capacity; China rejected Washington's overcapacity allegations as political manipulation while stopping short of retaliation, facing a capped rate of 20 per cent under an expiring truce that could rise to 40 per cent if it unravels. Vietnam sought to quickly conclude a trade deal—its US is its largest export market—to avoid rates rising from 20 per cent (if agreed) to 35 per cent, and committed to reforms including curbing forced-labour imports; Taiwan expressed confidence that Washington would maintain the previously agreed 15 per cent rate protecting semiconductors accounting for more than 70 per cent of its US-bound exports. South Korea said it would hold further talks while arguing excess capacity does not apply, facing a capped rate between 15 and 25 per cent; India rejected overcapacity claims and expects rates to be capped at 17 per cent if a deal is struck (up from an earlier reduction of most Indian tariffs from 50 per cent to 18 per cent). The proposed duties would not take effect until after a Jan 25 public hearing, though actual rates could fall below the maximum under existing or ongoing trade agreements.
items.title: Asian governments push back, seek deals after Trump's new tariff salvo

visual.alt: Bar chart. China (truce intact) 20 %; Singapore 20 %; Vietnam (deal reached) 20 %; India (deal struck) 17 %; South Korea 70 %.

items.summary: Hawkish Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said the central bank must respond swiftly to signs of inflation overshooting its target, including by accelerating interest rate hikes — keeping alive prospects of a rate increase as soon as December. Speaking on Thursday ahead of the BOJ's two-day policy meeting ending December 18, when markets widely expect the central bank to raise its policy rate from the current 1.25 per cent to 1.5 per cent, Tamura warned that rising raw material costs — including higher crude oil prices tied to a Middle East conflict — are pushing up goods prices with intensifying pass-through to consumer inflation ahead. He cited further upside risks to inflation from the Middle East war, higher import costs stemming from a weak yen, and still-robust demand for AI-related goods. Tamura argued that because underlying inflation is less firmly anchored at the BOJ's 2 per cent target than in other economies, Japan must respond more swiftly and strongly to price shocks; he said financial conditions remain accommodative and urged bringing the policy rate to a level deemed neutral soon. The remarks come after the BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25 per cent in September following a June hike — a shorter interval than the roughly twice-a-year hikes seen in 2024 and 2025 — while keeping rates steady in October even as underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2 per cent target.
items.title: BOJ Hawk Signals Faster Rate Hikes Ahead of December Meeting

items.summary: A political cartoon by Ben Jennings satirizes Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham in connection with assistance for winter fuel bills. The item is presented as a single cartoon without additional descriptive content, so no further substantive claims or evidence can be drawn from the source text.
items.title: Ben Jennings Cartoon Depicts Andy Burnham's Help With Winter Fuel Bills

items.summary: A projected 26% rise in energy bills from January, driven by a surge in gas prices linked to the Iran war, has prompted fears of hardship for many households. The government plans to pay £100 per household from 4 January and relies on an existing electricity VAT cut to help cover winter costs, but residents in Stockton-on-Tees and Darlington said this would not offset a rise of about £440 annually. Kathleen Simms of Stockton warned she might end up in hospital if she cannot afford heating, while Alexandra Blowers—who benefits from solar panels—said she still expected to limit her use of heat. Tim Robinson noted he was shielded by a fixed-rate deal but expressed concern for others who would not be so protected. Staff at Stockton Citizens' Advice anticipated increased demand for services as people in debt turn to support, with CEO Sarah McPhie noting that 70% of children growing up in poverty in the Tees Valley come from working households whose wages are unlikely to rise alongside energy prices.
items.title: UK Energy Bill Hike Sparks Winter Hardship Fears

items.summary: Judges overseeing the corruption trial of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu recommended that prosecutors drop the most serious charge, a development described as boosting the embattled Israeli leader and bringing the six-year case closer to resolution. In response Wednesday, Netanyahu said 'the trial has fallen,' characterizing the judges' remarks as 'a ray of truth and justice.' The judicial intervention arrives amid political shifts in Israel: opposition parties secured their first coalition partner, moving them closer to forming a government that would exclude Netanyahu, while lawmakers advanced an amendment designed to prevent him from reentering government. Commenting on this backdrop, The Economist's Israel correspondent argued it is 'absurd' for the country to focus so heavily on one individual's political survival and urged Israel to move past what they called its obsession with 'Bibi.'
items.title: Netanyahu Corruption Trial Judges Recommend Dropping Most Serious Charge

items.summary: The US economy grew at a rapid annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, even as inflation remained elevated and tech markets experienced a downturn. ING's chief international economist noted that falling gas prices combined with strong growth and inflation still deemed
items.title: US Economy Expanded 4.3% in Third Quarter Amid Elevated Inflation

items.summary: The UK private rental market has become intensely competitive, with rising prices and a shrinking supply of available rooms. In major cities, prospective tenants frequently compete against dozens of applicants for a single room, while potential housemates are imposing increasingly specific and unusual demands. A media outlet is soliciting personal accounts from people who have experienced this situation, specifically asking whether they sent numerous applications without success, endured lengthy interviews or flatmate 'auditions' to secure housing, or encountered bizarre or restrictive rules—such as bans on working from home or strict requirements around profession and lifestyle. The publication also asks how these experiences affected applicants' finances and wellbeing.
items.title: UK Renters Face Intensifying Competition for Private-Rental Rooms

items.summary: This weekend, 59% of consumers plan to use AI to support their winter shopping, according to the National Retail Federation. Despite that optimism, experts warn these tools make mistakes and demand sensitive personal data — two problems with meaningful stakes when holiday purchases are involved. Forrester analyst Emily Pfeiffer advises treating AI searches like a conversation with a young child: describe needs in terms of use case rather than exact specifications, since agents work better with hand-holding but can still misinterpret requests. Newer AI models go further by actually shopping for users — monitoring email to track packages and even completing purchases — which requires granting access to sensitive data such as an inbox or credit card; Meta's platform Muse asks whether users want to connect their email and calendar, though Meta says it keeps information private and holds credit cards separately. Privacy concerns remain: Meta has faced accusations of improperly sharing user data in a 2022 case that settled for about $725 million without admitting wrongdoing, and users have reported agents acting without consent by sending home addresses or booking hotels. ACI Worldwide's Philip Bruno says he would share what he is shopping for but be careful with payment information, while experts caution against over-sharing details about other people so AI cannot build profiles of friends and family. On deals, Pfeiffer notes a common misconception that AI sees everything; in reality agents still need time to find the best prices and may not access every website — Amazon blocks Meta's Muse for failing to identify itself or alert Amazon beforehand. Visa recently released a report warning buyers about AI shoppers: testing different models, it found they failed to recommend a product meeting customer needs in 42% of test runs, with more than half still recommending mismatched products, underscoring the need to verify recommendations before purchase.
items.title: AI agents for Black Friday shopping carry real risks

visual.alt: Bar chart. Visa report (AI failure rate) (Proportion of test runs where AI failed to recommend a matching product) 42 %; National Retail Federation (AI adoption rate) (Share of consumers planning to use AI for winter shopping this weekend) 59 %.

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Wednesday that tariff wars and trade wars serve no one's interests, commenting in response to reports that the United States was set to announce tariffs on goods from China and other countries. Speaking at a regular news briefing, Guo reiterated that China's position on economic and trade issues with the United States is consistent and clear, adding that both sides should resolve such matters through consultation based on equality, respect, and mutual benefit. He also dismissed what he called the false proposition of overcapacity as a pretext for political manipulation, urging the two countries to work together to uphold the common understandings between their heads of state and preserve steady growth in China-US economic and trade relations.
items.title: China's Foreign Ministry Warns Tariff and Trade Wars Serve No One

items.summary: Gain City opened its new megastore in Tampines on Thursday, November 26, and is running a limited-time Black Fri-Yay sale through November 29 to celebrate the launch. The promotion spans multiple product categories including bedding, air conditioners, TVs, furniture, and more, with discounts such as up to 60 percent off selected bedding models (with a free triple upsize) plus an additional S$200 off selected OLED and QLED TVs. A store-exclusive Star Buys segment offers heavily discounted products from brands including Samsung, Acer, and Simmons going at prices while stocks last; featured items include the Samsung A11 Tablet at S$99 (usual price S$288), the LG 65-inch Nano UHD AI ThinQ TV at S$499 (S$1,049), the Asus Vivobook 16 laptop at S$1,399 (S$2,099), and the Simmons Havana queen-sized mattress at S$3,299 (S$7,199). Shoppers can also receive free gifts with qualifying purchases of participating brands and models — a Dyson Supersonic hair dryer or Eikou steam air fryer on a minimum spend of S$1,500, and a DJI Pocket 4 Creator Combo or Shark TurboBlade fan on a minimum spend of S$3,000. Additionally, every S$100 spent earns shoppers a chance to win a BYD Atto 3 Evo car. Kenny Teo, managing director of Gain City, said in a statement that while online shopping offers convenience, he believes there is still tremendous value in the in-store experience for big-ticket purchases such as televisions, refrigerators, and furniture, noting customers want to see products up close, compare options, and speak with staff before deciding. The megastore is located at 11 Tampines North Drive 5, Singapore 529485.
items.title: Gain City Opens Tampines Megastore with Black Fri-Yay Deals

items.summary: At its seventh Innovation and Intellectual Property Forum in Beijing on November 24, 2026, Huawei reported that it had held over 8,000 AI-related patents by the end of 2025. The company also announced that in 2025 it signed 20 new patent licensees across network and communications equipment, consumer electronics and computing, IoT, automotive, streaming, and semiconductors industries. By year-end 2025, Huawei had filed more than 450,000 patent applications and held more than 165,000 active granted patents worldwide. Its outbound patent licensing agreements have cumulatively exceeded US$6.9 billion in value, with 2025 patent licensing revenue of approximately US$800 million; by the end of that year its patented technologies had been deployed in more than 3.2 billion 5G devices, over 1.6 billion Wi-Fi consumer electronics devices, and more than 4.1 billion multimedia devices. Among active granted patents, wireless communications (41%), terminal hardware (16%), and AI and computing (13%) represent the largest shares. Huawei executives Alan Fan and Emil Zhang attributed these figures to sustained research and development investment.
items.title: Huawei Reports Over 8,000 AI Patents by End of 2025

items.summary: In response to Donald Trump's latest round of tariffs targeting 14 major trading partners, Brazil declared it would not yield to the threat, calling the unilateral decision an unacceptable action within ongoing bilateral negotiations. The government voiced particular concern over proposed higher import taxes on raw and refined sugar and a new 10% tariff on aircraft that would affect Embraer, while reserving the right to adopt retaliatory measures if tariffs were imposed illegally. China accused Washington of political manipulation, with its embassy spokesperson rejecting claims of industrial overcapacity as nonexistent and urging both sides to honor agreements reached between Trump and Xi Jinping; a foreign ministry official added that a tariff or trade war serves no party's interests. The US administration said the new duties would be consistent with prior trade deals and are being imposed under a law permitting tariffs against countries engaging in unreasonable or discriminatory practices, with Jamieson Greer noting many partners had adopted market-distorting practices. China faces the highest capped rate of 20%, which could stack on other import taxes for a total of 45%. The US-China trade truce reached last year is set to expire on 10 January 2027, and the administration proposes a broad exemption covering $30bn worth of Chinese goods. Other affected countries include Vietnam, India—which denied structural excess capacity—Taiwan, which expects to maintain its existing 15% tariff rate despite tech products accounting for over 70% of its US exports—and Japan, whose government called the proposed measure regrettable.
items.title: Brazil and China Reject Trump Tariff Threats Against 14 Trading Partners

items.summary: The Trump administration has threatened new tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan, the European Union and several Southeast Asian countries such as Singapore, Malaysia and Vietnam. The proposed duties range from headline rates of 20 per cent to 40 per cent (q3-q4), are not due to kick in until January after a period of consultation, and target what Washington terms excess industrial capacity. However, the US Trade Representative has given governments an out with potential lower rates if they enter or already have an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade; those without such agreements face higher penalties if negotiations fail. Vietnam faces 20 per cent capped at agreement versus 35 per cent if talks fail (q6-q7), India would see 17 per cent versus 25 per cent (q8-q9), and Singapore faces a principal tariff rate of up to 20 per cent without an agreement, matching the Southeast Asian region's highest rate. The European Commission expects any US measures against Europe to respect a 15 per cent ceiling agreed last year (q5). Among the 14 partners, Singapore stands out as one which has yet to negotiate a trade deal with the US despite having a free trade agreement and running a US trade surplus. Analysts note that this strategy of forcing trading partners to the negotiating table may not work as it once did given legal defeats — including February's Supreme Court ruling striking down Trump's 'Liberation Day' tariffs — and the likelihood these tariffs may not outlast the administration, which would be conducted under a Section 301 probe (q16).
items.title: Trump's New Tariff Threat Targets Trading Partners, with Singapore Facing the Highest Regional Rate

items.summary: At the 31st Session of the Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CSP-31) in The Hague, China urged Japan to accelerate the destruction of chemical weapons abandoned on Chinese territory, arguing that prolonged delays undermine efforts toward 'a world free of chemical weapons.' A side event titled 'Current Status and Challenges with Respect to the Destruction of the Chemical Weapons Abandoned by Japan on the Territory of China' drew more than 100 representatives from over 40 countries. According to the Chinese delegation, Japan has missed its destruction deadlines four times; a plan adopted in 2022 is due to expire in 2027 and risks being missed for a fifth time. The article reports that Japan's budget for addressing these weapons was cut by 22% this year compared with 2025, even as its defense budget rose. Shen Bo of China's Permanent Representation to the OPCW said growing international concern centers on delays and the risk of missing the 2027 deadline, calling on Japan to fulfill its obligations under the convention and increase investment in personnel, technology and funding while providing accurate information on burial sites. Vladimir Tarabrin of Russia described the issue as a legal and moral obligation for Japan, OPCW Director-General Sabrina Dallafior stressed it is part of eliminating chemical weapons worldwide, Alexander Lomanov said the abandoned weapons have caused serious problems for Chinese civilians, and Datuk Tan Teik Cheng of Malaysia's Chinese Association urged Japan to face its wartime aggression rather than evade its obligations.
items.title: China Urges Japan to Accelerate Destruction of Abandoned Chemical Weapons

items.summary: On November 25, 2026 (Wednesday), senior Communist Party of China official Cai Qi met with a delegation led by Jorge Luis Broche Lorenzo — member of the PCC Secretariat and head of its Economic Productive Department — in Beijing. Cai, who is on the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau and the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, said China wants to work with Cuba to implement the consensus reached by the two parties' top leaders, enhance high-level exchanges, strengthen practical cooperation, deepen governance-experience exchanges, improve multilateral coordination, and advance bilateral relations. He also briefed the Cuban side on the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC. Broche congratulated China on convening that session, thanked China for its assistance in Cuba's response to its current difficult situation, and said Cuba is willing to study and draw on the CPC's experience leading China's opening-up and economic and social development.
items.title: Senior CPC Official Cai Qi Meets Cuban Party Delegation in Beijing

items.summary: Macy's postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York from Thursday to Saturday because a powerful coastal storm is expected to bring winds and rain too dangerous for the giant balloons. Preparations had already begun when the forecast called for heavy rain and strong winds on Thursday, prompting parade executive producer Will Cross—speaking at a Wednesday news conference with city officials—to say that the safety of partners, participants and spectators was his top priority. The 100 inflatable balloons were scheduled to fly as part of the centennial celebration, which also included 10 new balloons such as one depicting Bluey wearing a crown; they will be deflated on Wednesday night and stored in New Jersey until Saturday's event. Macy's confirmed the rescheduled date and updated its website countdown clock accordingly. The storm prompted emergency declarations from Long Island, New York City and Westchester County under Governor Kathy Hochul, and across all 21 counties of neighboring New Jersey by Governor Mikie Sherrill beginning at 18:00 local time on Wednesday. The US National Weather Service issued a high wind warning for Thursday until 01:00 (06:00 GMT) Friday with gusts potentially reaching 60mph (97km/h), though the strongest winds are likely to come after the parade's original end; NBC said it would still air the 2025 parade on Thursday. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who will not attend due to scheduled surgery, confirmed that extreme weather forced the change and announced an expanded police presence along the route while noting no known credible threats.
items.title: Macy's Postpones Its 100th Thanksgiving Parade to Saturday Over Severe Weather

items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration halted departures bound for Miami International Airport after a FedEx aircraft overran the runway on Wednesday evening, arriving from Memphis. Departures were grounded just after 20:15 local time (01:15 GMT), and all but one runway at the airport was closed according to the FAA advisory; flights are expected to resume by around 22:00 local time. No injuries have been reported, and the FAA is investigating the incident. The ground stop occurred on the day before Thanksgiving, which the American Automobile Association lists among the busiest travel days of the year in the US, with Miami being one of the top five domestic destinations for travelers during this holiday week. Flight delays reached about one hour but appeared to be declining later Wednesday night, and passengers were encouraged to check directly with their airlines for updates. The airport's spokesman Greg Chin said the department appreciates passenger patience as it works to safely resume normal operations.
items.title: FedEx Runway Overrun Grounds Miami Flights Before Thanksgiving

items.summary: Spanish Socialist leader Pedro Sánchez, who has held power for eight years as an icon of the European left while championing immigration and standing up to Donald Trump, may be replaced by a conservative government aligned with the far right following Sunday's pivotal election. The event is being reported by BBC Madrid correspondent Sam Jones and European community affairs correspondent Ashifa Kassam, who examine Sánchez's gamble in calling the vote; Nosheen Iqbal explores what the outcome means for the left in Spain and across Europe.
items.title: Spain's Election: Pedro Sánchez Faces Possible Conservative Succession

items.summary: Separatist and al-Qaida-affiliated insurgents in Mali have begun employing kamikaze quadcopter drones to attack the Malian army and its Russian paramilitary backers, mirroring drone tactics developed during the war in Ukraine. First-person-view footage of these off-the-shelf drones targeting Russians has become common as the conflict intensifies. The videos were captured by separatists and an al-Qaida affiliate during their joint assault on Mali's military forces and Russian mercenaries in April, showing a quadcopter locking onto a Russian vehicle while another drone struck three men identified as Russians near an airfield. According to these accounts, battlecraft refined within Ukraine has become a significant factor driving the resurgence of rebel activity across the Sahel.
items.title: Malian Rebels Use Commercial Drones Against Russian Forces

items.summary: On Wednesday, U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper of Washington, D.C., issued an injunction blocking enforcement of President Donald Trump's August executive order that limits the number of people eligible for birthright citizenship. The ruling came in a class action lawsuit filed on behalf of children who would be denied citizenship under the order, which Trump signed after the U.S. Supreme Court rejected his initial effort to impose restrictions. Judge Cooper is the second federal judge to block the order; another federal judge in Maryland also blocked it in September. The injunction will stymie what critics call a flagship part of the administration's hard-line immigration crackdown, and the administration would now need to overturn both court decisions before being able to enforce the executive order.
items.title: Second Judge Blocks Trump's Birthright Citizenship Executive Order

items.summary: Auburn police thwarted an attempted kidnapping of a man in Sydney's west by dramatically arresting four balaclava-clad men after their sedan collided with two vehicles on Olympic Drive in Lidcombe, injuring one person. About 5pm Wednesday, three allegedly armed men tried to enter an occupied SUV on Gormley Avenue; the driver reversed through a fence and fled while the attackers left in what police said was a stolen Mercedes. Traffic officers attempted to stop it before the crash, after which all four occupants — aged 22, 23, 25 and 38 (q2) — were arrested with assistance from Public Order and Riot Squad, Burwood Police Area Command and Raptor Squad officers. A witness, Tanya Hamilton, whose CCTV captured the incident, described seeing two men in black balaclavas run down her street before being
items.title: Four Men Charged After 'Crash Tackle' Arrest in Attempted Kidnapping; Ten Others Arrested in Drug Network

items.summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) has sued insurance giant AIG's subsidiary, AIG Australia — which offers travel and consumer device insurance — alleging it failed to respond to or notify customers of delays within the required 30-day timeframe in 534 general insurance complaint cases. ASIC commissioner Alan Kirkland said policyholders should not have to fight their insurer for basic communication, and alleged some customers waited months for decisions while unwell, injured, or recently bereaved between October 2021 and December 2025, with some given inaccurate explanations for the delays. The regulator alleges AIG used a standard template that pre-populated 'complexity' as the reason for delay, failed to inform customers of their rights to escalate complaints to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA), and lacked an effective system for recording complaint information or alerting staff when responses were due. ASIC is seeking declarations, pecuniary penalties, adverse publicity orders, and a requirement that AIG engage an independent expert to review its complaints-handling arrangements. The action follows weeks after the federal court fined Hollard $2 million (q5) for delaying processing of a home insurance claim until a house in regional Victoria became uninhabitable — the first civil penalty ordered against an insurer for breaching its duty of utmost good faith under the Insurance Contracts Act, which ASIC had sued over in April 2024. The broader context includes December 2024 (d7), when ASIC put general insurers on notice after reviewing 11 insurers (q8) and finding they failed to identify one in six complaints alongside shortcomings in customer communications and complaints-handling systems.
items.title: ASIC Sues AIG Australia Over Complaints-Handling Failures

items.summary: Under European Council President Antonio Costa's compromise proposal for financing the bloc's new seven-year budget, a mix of Europe-wide taxes is expected to generate about €60bn in revenue each year. Between 2028 and 2034, Germany would pay by far the highest share at over €13bn in current prices, followed by Italy with €8bn; France ranks third despite being the bloc's second-largest economy, which explains Paris' support for new own resources. The e-waste tax of €2.25 per kilogram is expected to yield more than any other levy—over €20bn annually—and over 60% of its revenues would come from Germany, Italy and France as manufacturing powerhouses, while Bulgaria would pay zero. Revenues are not fixed: the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) could more than double by 2034, and several taxes will be adjusted for inflation. For plastic packaging waste tax at €1.25 per kilogram and an EU-wide digital services tax—where France, Italy and Spain already have national levies—they would account for over 60% of revenues; the four largest member states (France, Germany, Italy and Spain) make up more than half of plastic-packaging-tax revenue.
items.title: Germany Would Pay the Most of New EU Taxes Under Costa's Proposal

items.summary: US President Donald Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte held a closed-door meeting at Mar-a-Lago in Florida on Wednesday that the White House called an "outstanding" and "very impactful" discussion. According to a joint statement released by the White House, the two leaders focused primarily on the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in Iran, reviewing progress from NATO summits held in The Hague and Ankara, Türkiye. They also discussed the importance of preventing Russia from expanding the war and achieving a rapid peaceful resolution. Additionally, Trump and Rutte reviewed plans to increase defense spending and investment in the defense industrial base across both the US and NATO member countries.
items.title: Trump and NATO Chief Discuss Ukraine, Iran, Defense Spending

items.summary: At its Nov. 16-23 meeting in Vilamoura, Portugal, the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas (ICCAT) adopted a compromise measure on shark finning that could establish a fins-naturally-attached rule by 2029 or 2030 under conditions, while allowing alternatives for frozen sharks. The deal was introduced by Japan and drew mixed reactions: the EU called it a landmark agreement, but conservationists criticized its complexity and lengthy timeline. Despite intense negotiations, parties failed to agree on a new catch limit or allocation system for yellowfin tuna—which has been fished above its 110,000-metric-ton annual total allowable catch in 13 of the last 15 years—and also failed to set management objectives for blue sharks. In other outcomes, ICCAT agreed to increase bigeye tuna catches by 16.4% and reduce southern albacore catches by 13.1%, adopted a rule requiring disclosure of chartered vessel beneficial owners, and kept the yellowfin FAD closure at 45 days for 2027.
items.title: ICCAT Adopts Compromise Shark Finning Rule While Failing to Set Yellowfin Catch Limits

items.summary: Indonesia's super El Niño-fueled dry season exposed roughly 12.5 million people to fire and smoke between January and September this year, according to the Indonesian Ministry of Health (q8). In Kalimantan alone, about 684,000 hectares burned — 36% of the national total despite covering just 28% of Indonesia's land area (q2, q4) — while NASA satellite data showed fires continuing even as rain arrived and hotspots shifted to drier areas. Facing intensifying seasons driven by climate change, communities in Kalimantan are turning to fire-free agriculture: a Planet Indonesia program is training farmers in West Kalimantan's Ketapang district through agroforestry on fallow land, with trained farmers becoming mentors (Runtu), while Gawi Bapakat — part of Kaleka NGO — launched its fire-free agriculture program in Seruyan in 2024 to help six Indigenous Dayak villages adopt non-burning techniques including organic fertilizer and multiple planting cycles. Participant Yadi reported a single unburned plot could yield up to four harvests, potentially three times the output of burned land (though drought affected productivity), and his first patchouli harvest in June 2026 produced 62 kilograms from an agroforestry plot (q10, q11). Yet practitioners note that while farmers report benefits, wider adoption requires government support; Gawi Bapakat's Anindya Hadi said budget cuts under austerity measures have constrained expansion despite community readiness. Researchers also found fire activity is concentrated in licensed oil palm areas — 63% of recent fires (q13) — with SIAR mapping showing most hotspots recur within previously burned peatland totaling about 500,000 hectares over the past decade.
items.title: Fire-free agriculture gains traction in Kalimantan amid El Niño-driven fire crisis

items.summary: Five-time Olympic gold medalist and presidential candidate Teddy Riner declared on Wednesday that he did not understand why France was sending troops to Ukraine, stating that the deployment of soldiers without prior public knowledge 'smelled bad.' When asked about France's solidarity with a European country, Riner questioned whether Ukraine is part of the European Union. His comments came more than a week after a source disclosed to French media that foreign soldiers had been deployed on a secret training mission in Ukraine for several months to train personnel and help maintain equipment. Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told reporters during a press conference that this amounted to 'direct participation in the war, including target designation assistance, satellite data provision, and other forms of support.' France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot subsequently denied allegations of direct involvement, underlining that the country was not involved in a military operation but rather in 'training and maintenance, carried out far from the front lines, with very limited scope and no involvement in warfare.' In early November, the European Council extended Europe's Military Assistance Mission to Ukraine for a further two years. According to a poll published by Elabe on 14 November, Riner is polling around 4.5%, trailing behind Marine Le Pen of the National Rally party and Jean Luc Mélenchon of France Unbowed.
items.title: Teddy Riner Says Ukraine Is Not France's War

items.summary: A Western Cape high court ruled Wednesday in favour of South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa, overturning a 2022 report that had found he may have a case to answer over the theft of large sums of foreign currency from his private farm. The complaint originated with a former spy boss and ally of Jacob Zuma, who alleged Ramaphosa hid a robbery of $4 million from police and tax authorities; separately, an independent parliamentary panel accused him of concealing a 2020 break-in and theft of $580,000 stashed in furniture at his Phala Phala farmhouse in Limpopo. Judge Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana declared the report unlawful, ruling that the panel
items.title: South African Court Overturns Impeachment Report Against Ramaphosa

items.summary: Uganda qualified for the FIFA U-17 World Cup round of 32 with a commanding 6-0 win over New Caledonia. Attacking midfielder Ismael Magala said the team's early-scoring plan worked as intended, noting they scored inside the first five minutes and added more before half-time; in the second half they pushed to score further for security. Head coach Laryea Kingston praised his players for responding under pressure and called the result
items.title: Uganda Advance to U-17 World Cup Round of 32 After 6-0 Victory Over New Caledonia

items.summary: Mahdi Tunsi, a 26-year-old Palestinian sociology and criminology student at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and known left-wing activist for Jewish–Arab relations, was arrested on November 8 after Israeli security forces entered his dormitory; neither he nor authorities informed his family until they reported him missing. He has remained in administrative detention—detention that can extend without trial or formal charges—for about two weeks as of a closed Tuesday hearing at the Jerusalem District Court, where prosecutors allege only
items.title: Palestinian Student Mahdi Tunsi Held in Administrative Detention Without Charge

items.summary: A female Spix's macaw (Cyanopsitta spixxi) named Hope was born at the São Paulo Zoo, marking progress for a species that has been extinct in the wild in Brazil for more than two decades. The chick weighs 350 grams and is one of barely 330 individuals left worldwide, which survive only in captivity after disappearing from northeastern Brazil's savannas in the 2000s. Raising Hope proved difficult: her egg required 26 days at 37.5 degrees Celsius with humidity between 40 and 45 percent before she needed to be broken out of the shell, and she initially refused syringe feeding until being fed through a tube for about 15 days. The species' fragile health stems from inbreeding and low reproduction among its few remaining members, so conservationists maintain detailed family trees to select breeding pairs. A turning point came in August 2023 when 27 birds arrived from a private facility that had left the national plan after infecting other birds with a virus during an earlier failed reintroduction attempt; these animals are state-owned and cannot be sold or exchanged outside Brazil. Chief bird biologist Fernanda Guida said conservationists aim to increase breeding pairs, ideally reaching about 10 but considering just two would already count as victory, before releases into Curaçá in Bahia's native habitat can be reconsidered.
items.title: São Paulo Zoo's Spix's macaw chick 'Hope' marks a milestone in Brazil's comeback effort

items.summary: On Wednesday (November 25), five international cooperation agreements were signed on the sidelines of the 12th World Halal Summit and Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Halal Expo in Istanbul. Türkiye's Halal Accreditation Agency (HAK) agreed to strengthen collaboration with Vietnam's Commission for Standards, Metrology and Quality; SMIIC reached an agreement with a Vietnamese authority during the program; SMIIC signed with the Kyrgyz Republic's Center for the Development of the Halal Industry under its Ministry of Economy and Commerce; the Saudi Halal Center held a signing ceremony with the Kyrgyz Republic to expand international alignment in halal standards and certification; and the Qatar Chamber of Commerce signed an agreement with the World Halal Summit Council. The summit opened Wednesday at the Istanbul Expo Center under President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's auspices, coordinated by the Turkish Trade Ministry, hosting 225 companies from 25 countries (q3: 225 companies, q4: 25 countries). Organized by Discover Events with SMIIC and Lokman Hekim University under the theme
items.title: Five Halal Cooperation Agreements Signed at Istanbul Summit

items.summary: WhatsApp announced a new global feature allowing users to schedule messages from 10 minutes ahead up to 14 days in advance, with delivery times chosen directly within existing conversations by holding the Send button and selecting a date. The company stated that scheduled text, photos, and videos will reach recipients at the set time even if the sender's phone is switched off or its battery dies, removing reliance on an active device. WhatsApp confirmed that these messages will receive end-to-end encryption identical to regular personal chats, meaning only the sender and recipient can read them while WhatsApp itself cannot access their contents. The company said the feature could help with birthday wishes, anniversary greetings, work reminders, announcements, and messaging contacts across time zones, though it noted availability may vary during rollout over coming weeks.
items.title: WhatsApp Rolls Out Scheduled Messages With Encryption

items.summary: The RBI's latest half-yearly report shows India repatriated around 60 tonnes of gold during April-September 2026, bringing total domestic holdings to 740.13 metric tonnes — or 84% of the country's 880.52-metric-tonne gold reserves at end September (with 140.39 tonnes held abroad). However, despite this increase in domestically held gold, its share of total foreign exchange reserves fell to 14.38% from 16.7% six months earlier; the domestic proportion had been 77% in March. India's overall forex reserves reached $705.3 billion at end September (up $46.67 billion over April-September, rising from $691.11 billion to $737.78 billion), covering about 9.8 months of imports when they stood at $668.6 billion in June; the short-term-debt-to-reserves ratio rose to 23% by end June (from 21.6%), and volatile-capital-flows-to-reserves reached 68% from 66.6%. Global gold prices fell roughly 9%, averaging $4,721 per troy ounce in April versus $4,319 in September, the report attributed to rising US Treasury yields, a stronger dollar, and tighter monetary-policy expectations.
items.title: RBI Repatriates ~60 Tonnes of Gold; Domestic Share Rises to 84% While Overall Reserve Share Falls

visual.alt: Bar chart. Held within India 740.13 metric; Held abroad (Bank of England & BIS) 140.39 metric.

items.summary: On X, Google CEO Sundar Pichai shared a Thanksgiving-themed web game called One More Pie, a 3D stacker built with Playground — an experimental browser-based platform that lets users create games from natural-language prompts. He linked the game to the tradition of piling dessert onto one plate and revealed his own high score under the username Planetarycode159, challenging others to beat it. In separate posts he announced that Google's Neon (Gemini 4 Neon) set a new Day-1 usage record on its paid APIs and reported that daily Antigravity token usage rose by 82% since Argon launched just six weeks ago; Elon Musk responded with the comment
items.title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai Shares Thanksgiving Game and Reports Neon API Usage Growth

visual.alt: Bar chart. Antigravity tokens/day change (Pichai's report) 82 %; Daily token usage rise (rephrased) (Pichai's report) 82 %; Antigravity tokens/day change (quoted post) (Pichai's quoted post) 82 %.

items.summary: The Chamber of Trading Industry (CTI) has urged the Indian government to consider imposing a 25 per cent retaliatory tariff on US goods if Washington proceeds with higher duties on Indian products. CTI Chairman Brijesh Goyal said in a video statement that traders are writing to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking reciprocal action, warning that the proposed measures could affect exports worth $48 billion and put around five lakh jobs at risk. Goyal cited concerns about sectors including pharmaceuticals, electronics, seafood, gems and jewellery, leather, metals and auto components, noting tariffs would make Indian goods more expensive for American buyers and prompt them to shift orders to competing countries. He also raised questions over consignments already dispatched to the US and orders placed with Indian exporters regarding how these shipments would be treated if tariffs take effect.
items.title: India's Chamber of Trading Industry Urges 25% Retaliatory Tariff on US Goods

items.summary: According to data released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on Wednesday, US inflation measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose to 3.8% year-on-year in October 2026, while core inflation—excluding volatile food and energy prices—stood at 3.3%. The BEA reported these figures in its Personal Income and Outlays report for October 2026, noting that the headline reading remained significantly above the Federal Reserve's target of 2%, which is the central bank's preferred measure tracked closely for monetary policy decisions. On a monthly basis, headline inflation moderated to 0.3% from 0.5% in September, while core inflation held steady at 0.3%. The report attributed the USD 63.8 billion increase in current-dollar PCE during October to gains of USD 11.8 billion in goods spending and USD 52.1 billion in services spending; however, real (inflation-adjusted) PCE declined by $5.8 billion—less than 0.1% at a monthly rate—signaling weakness in actual consumption despite rising nominal expenditure. Meanwhile, consumer spending growth slowed to 0.3% from 0.6%, even as personal income growth accelerated to 0.7% and disposable personal income rose by USD 200.5 billion (0.8%). Personal savings reached USD 1 trillion with a saving rate of 4.1%. The persistence of inflation above the Fed's target, combined with slowing consumer spending growth, presents a challenge for policymakers balancing price stability against economic growth.
items.title: US October Inflation Rises to 3.8%, Nearly Double the Fed's Target

items.summary: The Trump administration's USTR announced a proposed 25 per cent tariff (q1, q2) on India based on alleged excess industrial structural capacity. The rate would fall to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a bilateral trade deal (q3, q8). This proposal is part of a Section 301 investigation into manufacturing output across 14 economies (q4, q6), which include China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia, Singapore and Switzerland. The probe began last March after the US Supreme Court overturned tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act; India faces a separate 100 per cent tariff risk (q7) from an unrelated Russia sanctions bill. USTR official Jamieson Greer said the proposed duties would generally not stack on existing ones and instead act as a top-up of a few percentage points, with public hearings scheduled for January 25 and written comments due by January 5. India's Commerce Ministry rejected the rationale, stating that it has no structural excess capacity in any sector and that trade concerns should be handled through negotiations toward an early conclusion of the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement.
items.title: US Proposes 25% Tariff on India Over Excess-Capacity Claim; New Delhi Rejects Rationale

items.summary: Washington's new tariff proposals have introduced uncertainty into India-US trade relations. The US Trade Representative suggests a 17 per cent tariff on Indian imports if a trade agreement is finalised, which could rise to 25 per cent otherwise. Washington claims India's industrial policies cause structural excess capacity and limit opportunities for American businesses, while the Commerce Department states no such excess exists; India denies these claims. Ongoing negotiations on tariff relief and market access face added pressure, with officials urging India to prepare and diversify.
items.title: New US Tariff Proposals Bring Uncertainty to India-US Trade Talks

items.summary: NCP (SP) national working president Supriya Sule adopted a more conciliatory position toward the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, telling news agency PTI that it would be premature to oppose the legislation before its details are known and suggesting there could be something good in it. She argued against both blindly opposing bills as an opposition party and uncritically supporting them simply because one is in power, stating her party would discuss the bill once introduced and support it if it served national interests. Her remarks come amid broader resistance from the opposition to the NDA government's delimitation push. Sule also dismissed speculation about her faction joining the BJP-led NDA or her securing a ministerial position at the Centre or Maharashtra chief ministership as gossip, noting she has been a minister for 12 years and since 2014. Separately, she ruled out any merger between the two NCP factions led by Sharad Pawar and his nephew Ajit Pawar, stating that possibility ended with Ajit Pawar's death in an air crash.
items.title: NCP (SP) Leader Supriya Sule Softens Stance on Delimitation Bill Amid Political Speculation

items.summary: Members of the DMK student wing hung an effigy of Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh from a bridge in Vandavasi, Tiruvannamalai district, on Thursday, staging a demonstration that recreated a scene from actor-politician Vijay's film Theri. The protesters demanded his arrest over a sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman district collector against him for allegedly sending inappropriate messages. They raised slogans calling for the MLA's detention and cited Tamil Nadu's Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, along with relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to sexual harassment, stalking, and assault or criminal force against a public servant.
items.title: DMK Student Wing Hangs Effigy of TVK MLA Over Sexual Harassment Complaint

items.summary: Epochal, a new startup founded by three former xAI co-founders—Guodong Zhang, Zihang Dai, and Manuel Kroiss—who left after Elon Musk merged xAI with SpaceX in February, aims to build an AI model capable of predicting future events. The company describes its initial product as a "time portal" that lets AI agents browse archived versions of the internet from specific dates, intending this capability to simulate the past and teach AI to forecast the future. Epochal states it seeks to create a decision-making tool grounded in what it calls "superhuman prediction," arguing that because every decision is fundamentally a prediction, such technology could redefine nearly all industries. Zhang is personally investing $100 million into the company, per an anonymous source familiar with the matter; the information is not public and Epochal declined to comment on funding. The startup's team also includes former employees from xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind. Epochal distinguishes itself by offering "point-in-time" search queries that it claims deliver greater accuracy than other startups attempting similar predictive AI systems.
items.title: Three ex-xAI Founders Launch Epochal to Predict the Future

items.summary: The Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry rejected the United States Trade Representative's (USTR) determination charging India with structural excess capacity, stating that trade concerns should be resolved through ongoing negotiations for an India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement rather than unilateral measures. The USTR determination is part of a broader investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity across 16 economies, though Washington has made formal determinations against only 14—including India, China, the European Union, and Japan—arguing that government policies distort global trade. In India's case, the USTR cited industrial expansion plans, inadequate labour protections, financial repression, barriers to market access, and identified pharmaceuticals/medical devices, steel, solar products, and ICT as sectors of particular concern. Proposed tariff rates vary across affected economies: Vietnam faces up to 35% (potentially reducible to 20%), China up to 20%, Singapore up to 20%, Bangladesh/Cambodia/Indonesia/Malaysia/Thailand up to 18%, and the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and Switzerland at 15%. The proposed rates follow the US Supreme Court's decision striking down Trump-era tariffs under IEEPA, prompting separate Section 301 investigations of alleged excess capacity. The determination is now in a public consultation phase, with written comments due by January 5, 2027, and hearings scheduled to begin on January 25.
items.title: India Rejects US Tariff Charge as Washington Proposes Duties Across Six Economies

items.summary: After a November 12-13 outage that lasted about 24 hours and hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States while delaying trading firms and disrupting airline communications, Microsoft declared a 'Code Red' drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures. The incident disrupted Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products, and M365 Core President Jason Henderson called it the most customer-impacting event in Exchange Online's history — never before had so many customers been without email for so long. CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized, and Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July rather than cyber activity or AI agents.
items.title: Microsoft Declares 'Code Red' After Historic Outage, Internal Memos Show

items.summary: On Thursday, November 26, Delhi's air quality reached the severe category with an AQI of 263 at 8:41 AM (US scale), down 71 points from an overnight peak of 334. The capital ranked 60th among the world's most polluted cities and faced a high risk of asthma symptoms, including wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and persistent cough; AQI.in advised people with asthma to stay indoors, keep windows closed, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and limit secondhand smoke exposure. Throughout November 25-26 the readings fluctuated widely: they fell to 165 at 5:01 PM on Wednesday (the lowest in the prior 24 hours), rose above 300 before midnight reaching 334 at 3:31 AM, stayed above 300 until after 5 AM, then eased. November's daily figures included a high of 666 on November 9 and 547 on November 12, with all 14 days in the first fortnight exceeding 300 (Wednesday at 226 down from Tuesday's 236; Monday at 311). The seven-day AQI peaked at 532 at 6 AM on November 19 and bottomed at 186 at noon on November 25. At the time of measurement, Delhi's PM10 was 261 micrograms per cubic metre—about 5.8 times the WHO guideline of 45—and its finer PM2.5 particles measured 186 micrograms per cubic metre (both in the unhealthy range), with carbon monoxide at 2,214 parts per billion and nitrogen dioxide at 20 parts per billion.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Reached Severe Levels on November 26

items.summary: Sri Lanka has temporarily waived prior Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) approval for Indian travellers, allowing them to visit without obtaining it until further notice due to maintenance of the system. High Commissioner Mahishini Colonné announced the change and asked travellers to accept any inconvenience caused. The relaxation aims to ease travel disruptions while the ETA system is maintained. Sri Lanka earlier this year launched a six-country tourism promotion campaign targeting Australia, China, Germany, the UK, Russia and India ahead of its long-delayed global campaign in April 2027, with deputy tourism minister Roshan Ranasinghe saying it aims to nearly double arrivals during peak winter season and earn $4.2 billion. Tourism is Sri Lanka's third-largest foreign exchange earner; the country recorded 1.3 million arrivals in the first seven months of this year after about a 20% decline in March and April due to the Gulf crisis, with tourism earnings at $1.5 billion by end July. The government revised its arrival target from 3 million to 2.7 million while expecting $4.2 billion in revenue, having earned $3.2 billion from tourism in 2025. Sri Lanka's foreign exchange reserves stood at $6.6 billion at the end of last month, and the Central Bank raised its key policy rate by 100 basis points to 8.75% in May partly to ease pressure on the rupee.
items.title: Sri Lanka Temporarily Waives ETA for Indian Travellers Amid Tourism Push

items.summary: On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly officially adopted India's Constitution. Eight decades later, it remains a young republic's defining document that has endured and grown alongside the country it helped shape. Unlike France, which wrote its constitutions long after nation formation and now counts five republican versions since 1958, India is among few countries where constitution-drafting coincided with nation-building; the Supreme Court has proposed an unamendable basic structure doctrine rooted in this history of anti-colonial struggle, dismantling feudal hierarchy, and envisioning an inclusive society. The first amendments passed by the provisional assembly are treated as part of the original text, a view the Supreme Court accepted to protect their meaning. India took its international place through constitutional processes: borrowing directive principles from Ireland but making them fundamental in governance, adapting U.S.-style due process into more complex provisions across preventive detention, property acquisition, and criminal trials, and using rule of law inherited from colonial rulers to dismantle caste and gender hierarchies while introducing affirmative action. The Constitution affirms the individual as its basic unit without erasing communities or groups, remains flexible enough for future change despite over 100 amendments—many contested, reversed by successive parliaments, or struck down by courts—and preserves structural features like a republican head, parliamentary form, and unified judiciary while balancing core values with innovation. Women's active participation in preceding movements contributed to universal adult franchise, rare among contemporary societies; the aspiration for equality extends beyond individuals to socially backward classes, Scheduled Tribes and Castes, and women, scaffolding later claims on disability and transgender rights within a 76-year-old framework without disrupting its core nature. The Preamble offers no reference to a glorious past or divine source—people are constitutional power's origin—and the framers' optimism about equality despite nation-forming difficulties and Partition violence reflects moral integrity imbibed into the text, making attempts to amend it in ways that do not enhance these values resistant as unconstitutional. Professor of Law Nimushakavi Vasanthi, Director of NALSAR University of Law's Centre for Constitutional Law, frames this combination of eternal values with contemporary democratic functioning as possibly explaining the Constitution's endurance.
items.title: India's Constitution at 77: Framers' Moral Integrity and Enduring Vision of Equality

items.summary: Cockroach Janta Party convenor and investigative journalist Saurav Das alleged late Wednesday that "certain BJP-aligned social media handles" had leaked his passport, calling it a serious concern. The claim came two days after he was stopped from travelling to the United Kingdom—where he was scheduled to speak at several universities about youth protests in India—for failing to respond to a show-cause notice issued through email just five hours before his flight. Earlier that day, the Ministry of External Affairs said it had issued Das a notice based on law enforcement reports "seeking his clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth," and he was advised not to use the passport until submitting his response. In his post, Das asked whether leaks of citizens' passports were routine and questioned whether doxing—publicly sharing private information online without consent—had been legalised in India; he said he would file a criminal complaint against all handles that circulated his passport. Das stated at a Tuesday press conference that the notice was issued by the regional passport office in Chennai over alleged discrepancies, gave no details of the claimed issues, and followed an October 30 Madras High Court order on a plea demanding investigation into his citizenship and background; the court had also sought cancellation of his passport if he were found to be a foreign citizen. Das noted his passport was issued in 2019. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the application process requires accurate information, confirming the notice asked why it should not be impounded given an alleged mismatch between documents submitted and Aadhaar. The Cockroach Janta Party had named Das as its chief spokesperson on June 3 ahead of a protest demanding resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over irregularities in competitive examinations; Pradhan resigned July 25 after the protests spread following a police crackdown in Delhi.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party's Saurav Das Blames BJP-Linked Handles for Leaked Passport

items.summary: On Thursday, November 26 (reported by PTI), Delhi recorded its coldest morning of the season so far with a minimum temperature of 9 degrees Celsius. The India Meteorological Department said this was 2.3 degrees below the seasonal average and forecast mist during the day with a maximum around 27 degrees Celsius. Air quality remained in the 'poor' category, with Delhi's Air Quality Index standing at 228. Under the Central Pollution Control Board classification cited by PTI, an AQI of 0–50 is 'good', 51–100 'satisfactory', 101–200 'moderate', 201–300 'poor', 301–400 'very poor', and above 400 'severe'.
items.title: Delhi Records Season's Coldest Morning at 9°C as Air Quality Stays 'Poor'

items.summary: On Constitution Day (November 26, 2026), Congress leader Rahul Gandhi posted on X that the Indian Constitution is 'the soul of India,' a shield protecting citizens' dignity, and pledged to fight for its protection; he described it as safeguarding justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. The Janata Dal (United) accused Congress of hypocrisy over planned vote-"chori" marches, with national spokesperson Rajeev Ranjan Prasad citing the Emergency, curtailment of civil liberties, and suppression of press freedom. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma called the Constitution a 'living sacred document' safeguarding citizens' rights. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced a 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' protest in Nagpur over alleged Election Commission irregularities; founder-convenor Abhijeet Dipke said CJP would also launch a six-day 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign across drought-affected districts of Vidarbha and Marathwada. Delhi Police denied permission for a Samyukta Kisan Morcha march to Jantar Mantar, stating no application was received and that Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, prohibits unauthorized gatherings in New Delhi district. The Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee will hold a 'Samvidhan Raksha March' starting at 12:15 pm from Chandgi Ram Akhara in Civil Lines; Uttarakhand's party plans a 'Samvidhan Bachao March' beginning at 11 am, protesting alleged corruption under the state BJP government and what it called an insult to the Constitution by the Central government.
items.title: Congress and SP Plan Nationwide Constitution Day Protests Against Election Commission

items.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) is set to launch its election manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls at a press conference at 4pm on Thursday, even as it continues seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress. The two parties began talks on Monday; on Tuesday the SP offered 26 seats to the Congress against the party's demand of 120 seats (with at least 50 'winnable' seats), and a second round of talks is scheduled for Friday, per HT reporting citing sources familiar with the details. The seat-sharing dispute surfaced after the SP released its first list of five candidates on Tuesday night—nominees in Saharanpur, Shamli, Amroha and Lalitpur comprising four Muslims and one non-Yadav OBC candidate—which Congress MP Imran Masood criticized as undermining the alliance's seriousness. Meanwhile, a newly formed Samajik Parivartan Morcha bloc of AIMIM and Chandra Shekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) named Azad as its CM face for all 403 seats in the polls; SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said 'winnability' would guide final seat distribution. The BJP, led by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and deputy Keshav Prasad Maurya, expressed confidence of winning but did not settle on a CM face—Adityanath declined to name one while Maurya suggested legislators could choose after the polls.
items.title: Samajwadi Party to Release UP Election Manifesto Amid Seat-Sharing Talks

items.summary: The National Security Guard (NSG), India's federal counter-terrorism force, has completed six weeks of police commando conversion courses for personnel from the anti-terror units of Maharashtra, Telangana, West Bengal, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh. The training is part of plans to ensure states have battle-ready commando teams capable of responding to a 26/11-type terror attack, officials aware of the programme said. A major focus of the course is hostage rescue during incidents such as those at the Taj Mahal Hotel during the Mumbai attacks, where teams had to check hundreds of rooms across multiple buildings while fighting was ongoing. Officials noted that state police anti-terror units have strong personnel but often specialize in intelligence gathering and investigating terror cases rather than direct combat operations. The Union home ministry is tracking these training programmes conducted at the NSG's Manesar headquarters, with plans for refresher courses once the first round concludes so all major states maintain dedicated first-responder teams even as the NSG expands its presence.
items.title: NSG Completes Six-Week Commando Training for Five State Anti-Terror Units

items.summary: This article presents 10 easy and unique dessert ideas designed to make a Thanksgiving table extra special, ranging from comforting pumpkin flavors to chocolatey treats and caramel delights.
